svg.title: QuantumOS: build and evaluate your fault-tolerant quantum operating system
svg.desc: Three layers. Top: fault-tolerant programs compiled through logical measurements and lattice surgery into a listing of system calls. Middle: the operating system interface, eight system calls (request_ancilla, route, gates, measure, decode_syndrome, request_magic, pauli_frame_update, release_ancilla), a scheduler, a machine that declares a latency and a capacity per service, and a resource VM that admits or refuses a program. Bottom: a real quantum computer simulated with its control system: RISC-Q control cores running RV32I firmware, a board hub, a decoder core and converters, driving superconducting transmons, trapped ions that shuttle, and neutral atoms carried by AOD tweezers. Measured costs flow back up to calibrate the machine.
svg.text: Fault-tolerant programs compiled down to system calls
algorithm → logical measurements → lattice surgery → system calls
only system calls reach the machine: a program never names a physical qubit or a path
The quantum operating system · system calls
the program says when · the machine says how long · the VM checks
